stories.title: JLL Lists Chelsea’s Rubin Museum for Sale
stories.excerpt: JLL has been retained by the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art to market its New York City flagship location for sale. Located at 140–154 W. 17th St. in Chelsea, the property represents a rare opportunity to reposition a historically and architecturally significant asset at the nexus of Chelsea, the Flatiron District and Greenwich Village, according to JLL. The 80,000-square-foot mixed-use site features a six-story former museum property totaling roughly 52,000 square feet, complemented by an adjacent and contiguous residential component with 46 apartments. “This is a truly one-of-a-kind asset in New York City,” said David Carlos, vice chairman and head of JLL’s Nonprofit, Education & Government Practice. “Its rich history, institutional-quality infrastructure and architectural character make it exceptionally well-suited for a variety of uses. Opportunities like this, where a property can seamlessly adapt to cultural, educational, commercial or mixed-use applications, are extraordinarily rare in today’s market.” The post JLL Lists Chelsea’s Rubin Museum for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL marketing Rubin Museum, 140–154 W. 17th St. Chelsea, 80K SF mixed-use.
Property includes 52K SF former museum plus 46 residential units contiguous.
Rare repositioning opportunity at Chelsea-Flatiron-Greenwich Village nexus.
stories.summary: JLL has been retained to sell the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art's flagship location in Chelsea, a rare 80,000-square-foot mixed-use asset comprising a 52,000-square-foot six-story former museum building adjacent to a 46-unit residential component. The property sits at a prime intersection of three major Manhattan neighborhoods and is described as exceptionally well-suited for cultural, educational, commercial, or mixed-use redevelopment. This is a potential adaptive-reuse play on a trophy trophy asset in one of Manhattan's most desirable submarkets.
stories.impact: The 46 embedded residential units and the likely conversion/expansion of residential uses on a high-profile, architecturally significant Chelsea site signals ongoing appetite for residential density in core Manhattan. For TCR, this underscores scarcity of large ground-up or adaptive-reuse multifamily opportunities in prime Manhattan neighborhoods; successful repositioning here (especially if residential footprint is materially expanded) will validate pricing and feasibility of mixed-use plays in high-barrier markets.

stories.title: Gantry Arranges Life Company Loan on Temecula Offices
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $9-million life company loan to retire a CMBS loan on Vail Ranch Town Square, a low-rise suburban office building located at 32605 Temecula Pkwy. in Temecula. Principal Tony Kaufmann and associates Toby Judge and Jake Davis with the firm’s San Francisco production office represented the borrower, a private real estate investor in Southern California. The fixed rate, three-year loan featured a rate lock at application that protected the borrower in a rising rate environment. Gantry will service the loan for the lender. The three-story, 55,000-square-foot, Mediterranean-style building is 100%-leased to a range of medical, dental, behavioral health and professional service tenants. The location offers abundant surface parking and ready access to nearby retail, dining, and residential neighborhoods. Kaufmann said, “The case for office continues to improve and Gantry’s roster of life company lenders are showing an increasing willingness to fund new loans on performing assets.” The post Gantry Arranges Life Company Loan on Temecula Offices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry arranged $9M life company loan, Vail Ranch Town Square, Temecula, CA.
55K SF, 100%-leased medical/dental/professional office; 3-year fixed rate loan.
Life company lenders showing increased willingness to fund performing office assets.
stories.summary: Gantry secured a $9 million fixed-rate life company loan for Vail Ranch Town Square, a fully leased 55,000-square-foot suburban office building in Temecula. The borrower refinanced out of a CMBS loan into a three-year life company instrument with a rate lock that protected against rising rates. The property is 100% leased to medical, dental, behavioral health, and professional service tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, the note that life company lenders are increasingly funding performing office assets signals a slight thaw in office financing after years of distress; this may reduce forced seller dynamics in some markets but does not directly move multifamily demand, supply, or capital flows. The story is office-focused.

stories.title: Brooklyn Navy Yard Brings New Rotation of Small Businesses to Yard Opportunity Shop
stories.excerpt: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation (BNYDC) announced the third rotation of small businesses at its Yard Opportunity Shop (YOS) storefront. Now entering its third season, the YOS x Made in NYC Bodega will bring Doosra, Gracie Baked, Live Loud Foods and Oso Cacao together under one roof. Hosted in Building 92 of the Brooklyn Navy Yard, the three-month YOS rotations give small, minority-and-women-owned businesses (MWBEs) the opportunity to promote their products, test new concepts and directly engage with the Brooklyn community. YOS is part of BNYDC’s growing pipeline of initiatives supporting local MWBE retail entrepreneurs. “New York’s food scene is one of the most dynamic in the world, driven by entrepreneurs who are constantly reimagining what a product, a menu or a business can be,” said Lindsay Greene, president and CEO of the BNYDC. “We want the Navy Yard to be a place where that kind of innovation has room to grow.” The post Brooklyn Navy Yard Brings New Rotation of Small Businesses to Yard Opportunity Shop appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brooklyn Navy Yard launches third rotation of small businesses at Yard Opportunity Shop.
YOS x Made in NYC Bodega features four MWBEs; three-month rotation model.
Part of BNYDC's retail pipeline supporting minority and women-owned entrepreneurs.
stories.summary: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation announced the third rotation of small businesses at its Yard Opportunity Shop storefront in Building 92, featuring four minority- and women-owned businesses (MWBEs) in food and beverage sectors. The three-month rotation model is designed to help small entrepreneurs test concepts, promote products, and engage with the Brooklyn community. This is part of a broader BNYDC initiative to support local MWBE retail entrepreneurs.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, continued activation and retail incubation at the Navy Yard (a major mixed-use development node in Brooklyn) suggests sustained neighborhood vitality and foot traffic, which can indirectly support multifamily demand in nearby residential markets as walkability and retail amenities compound. This is a weak signal.

stories.title: Value-Add Rentals Go for $13M in El Cajon
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 229 Shady Ln., a circa-1969, 59-unit multifamily property located in El Cajon. The asset sold for $13.25 million, or $224,576 per unit. “Value-add apartment communities in East County San Diego continue to attract investor interest because of strong renter demand, limited housing supply and opportunities to improve operations over time,” said Austin Huffman, senior director investments. “Villa Capri offered an attractive combination of spacious floor plans, upgraded property systems and meaningful rental upside, making it a compelling acquisition for an investor seeking long-term value.” Huffman and Christopher Zorbas, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s San Diego office, represented the seller, Mary Susan Curry 2020 Revocable Living Trust, and procured the buyer, TFT Capital I. The property is located near Interstate 8, the El Cajon Transit Center and major employment centers throughout San Diego County. The buyer plans to renovate the property to enhance its long-term value. The post Value-Add Rentals Go for $13M in El Cajon appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closed 229 Shady Ln., El Cajon, 59-unit value-add for $13.25M.
Sale price $224,576/unit; circa-1969 property; buyer TFT Capital I plans renovation.
East County San Diego renter demand strong; limited supply supports investor interest.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of Villa Capri, a 59-unit multifamily property in El Cajon built in 1969, for $13.25 million ($224,576 per unit). The buyer, TFT Capital I, plans to renovate and enhance the property. The transaction reflects strong renter demand, limited housing supply, and attractive value-add economics in East County San Diego near Interstate 8 and major employment centers.
stories.impact: Strong signal for East County San Diego multifamily demand and cap rate compression. Limited supply and sustained renter demand justify value-add acquisitions at sub-$225K/unit in a secondary submarket, indicating TCR should prioritize land and development opportunities in East County before comps reset higher. Secondary San Diego markets (El Cajon, Escondido, Oceanside) remain undersupplied relative to in-migration and job growth; ground-up development window is open before land values spike further.

stories.title: The Learning Experience Plans Expansion in NY Tri-State, Upstate NY
stories.excerpt: Childcare franchise The Learning Experience plans to add nine locations across the New York Tri-State area and five in Upstate New York over the next 18 months. The company currently operates 43 locations in the Tri-State region. Plans call for a new Learning Experience location in Fair Lawn, NJ during the fourth quarter of 2026. It will be followed by new sites in Monroe, CT (Q1 2027); Islip, NY (Q3 2027); Sparta, NJ (Q4 2027); Old Bridge, NJ (Q4 2027); Port Jefferson Station, NY (Q1 2028); East Meadow, NY (Q1 2028); Hauppauge, NY (Q1 2028); and Belleville, NJ (Q2 2028). In addition to the New York City market, The Learning Experience plans to open three new locations in the Syracuse area (Liverpool, Clay and Syracuse), one in Albany, and one near Buffalo in East Amherst. Those openings run from Q3 2027 through Q1 2028. Each location will consist of up to 10,000 square feet of indoor building space with up to a 5,000-square-foot playground. The post The Learning Experience Plans Expansion in NY Tri-State, Upstate NY appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Learning Experience plans 14 new childcare locations: 9 Tri-State (NJ/NY/CT), 5 Upstate NY.
Openings stagger Q4 2026–Q2 2028; Fair Lawn, Monroe, Syracuse, Buffalo, Albany targeted.
Each site ~10K SF building plus 5K SF playground; 43 existing Tri-State locations.
stories.summary: The Learning Experience, a childcare franchise, announced plans to open 14 new locations across the New York region over 18 months: nine in the Tri-State area (Fair Lawn, Monroe, Islip, Sparta, Old Bridge, Port Jefferson Station, East Meadow, Hauppauge, Belleville) and five in Upstate New York (Syracuse, Liverpool, Clay, Albany, East Amherst). Each location will occupy up to 10,000 square feet with a 5,000-square-foot playground. Phased openings run Q4 2026 through Q1 2028.
stories.impact: Childcare expansion signals confidence in population and family household growth across NY Tri-State and Upstate markets, a leading indicator of multifamily demand. For TCR: this childcare buildout is a proxy for demographic tailwinds; focus development in suburban NY submarkets where Learning Experience is locating (Fair Lawn, Sparta, Old Bridge in NJ; Islip, Port Jefferson, East Meadow, Hauppauge on Long Island; upstate Syracuse/Albany corridor). Childcare scarcity has been a headwind for family renter formation; expansion should unlock additional multifamily absorption.

stories.title: Distyl AI Doubles Its 135 Madison Offices to 30K SF After Less Than a Year
stories.excerpt: Software development company Distyl AI has room to grow. The artificial intelligence-powered developer of operating systems for large companies has leased the entire ninth floor at 135 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, according to building manager Koeppel Rosen, bringing the company’s total footprint to 30,076 square feet. Distyl AI arrived at the Rosen family’s 13-story building in December 2025, Commercial Observer reported at the time, initially taking 15,038 square feet across the entire 10th floor. Asking rent for the recent expansion was $55 per square foot, and both leases run through January 2028, according to Crain’s New York Business, which first reported the lease. Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel represented the Rosen family in the transaction, while Justin Pollner and Steven Rotter of Newmark negotiated on behalf of Distyl AI. Distyl AI’s arrival at 135 Madison in December represented the company’s first office in New York City and second location overall, after establishing its headquarters at 55 Hawthorne Street in San Francisco in 2022. “We were pleased to work with Distyl AI to reconfigure and expand its footprint across two contiguous floors at 135 Madison Avenue,” Koeppel said in a statement. “We celebrate the company’s rapidly growing operations, which required additional office space.” The office building on the corner of East 31st Street and Madison Avenue is also home to health care technology platform Courier Health, coworking firm WeWork, digital marketing firm Demand Growth Digital, e-commerce marketing company Mobikasa and event space provider Blender Workspace. A spokesperson for Distyl AI did not immediately respond to a requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Distyl AI doubled NoMad offices at 135 Madison Ave., Manhattan; 15K SF → 30K SF.
Leased entire 9th floor at $55/SF; total footprint 30,076 SF; lease through Jan 2028.
Tech company expanded within <1 year of initial December 2025 arrival in NYC.
stories.summary: Software developer Distyl AI leased the entire ninth floor at 135 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood, doubling its footprint from 15,038 to 30,076 square feet less than one year after its initial December 2025 arrival in New York. Asking rent for the expansion was $55 per square foot, with both leases running through January 2028. The company's second-ever location (after San Francisco HQ) signals strong NYC expansion momentum.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, rapid office expansion by an AI-powered software company in Manhattan's NoMad neighborhood signals sustained tech talent in-migration and wage growth in NYC, which underpins multifamily renter demand and rent growth in Manhattan and nearby outer-borough submarkets. For TCR: NoMad and adjacent neighborhoods (Flatiron, Kips Bay) remain strong anchors for multifamily development; continued tech hiring will support premium rental absorption and pricing power.

stories.title: CIP Real Estate Buys San Gabriel Valley Industrial Park for $61M
stories.excerpt: The owner of a 200,049-square-foot industrial and flex complex in Los Angeles County’s San Gabriel Valley has unloaded the asset for $60.7 million. The Irvine-based CIP Real Estate acquired the Walnut Tech Business Center, an 11-building property at Valley Boulevard and Lemon Avenue in Walnut, from an affiliate of AEW. The complex contains 109 industrial, flex-office and service-commercial suites ranging from 640 to 8,400 square feet and is 92 percent leased. Property records show City National Bank provided $42.9 million in acquisition financing, arranged by JLL. CIP also plans a $3.5 million capital improvement program this year. The business center sits about a mile from the 60 Freeway and serves the City of Industry area, where small bay industrial space remains highly supply constrained. “Very few quality small bay industrial parks come available for sale in Southern California each year, especially a best-in-class project in this strategically important submarket of L.A. County,” CIP CEO Eric Smyth said in a statement. CIP represented itself in the transaction, while JLL’s Patrick Nally, Evan Moran and Chad Solomon represented AEW. The Walnut acquisition extends a busy stretch for CIP. The firm said it has closed more than $200 million in industrial park transactions over the past 90 days across Dallas, South Florida and Atlanta, bringing its industrial portfolio to more than $2.5 billion. The company owns and manages more than 12 million square feet of real estate. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIP Real Estate acquired Walnut Tech Business Center, San Gabriel Valley, for $60.7M.
200K SF, 11-building industrial/flex complex; 109 suites; 92% leased; $3.5M capex planned.
Walnut location ~1 mile from 60 Freeway; small-bay industrial remains supply-constrained.
stories.summary: CIP Real Estate, based in Irvine, acquired Walnut Tech Business Center, a 200,049-square-foot industrial and flex complex in Walnut, California, from an AEW affiliate for $60.7 million. The 11-building property contains 109 suites (640–8,400 SF) and is 92% leased. City National Bank provided $42.9 million in acquisition financing arranged by JLL. CIP plans a $3.5 million capital improvement program.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, strong small-bay industrial demand and supply scarcity in LA County's San Gabriel Valley (Walnut, City of Industry area) reflects sustained logistics and light manufacturing activity, signaling job stability and wage growth in that submarket. For TCR: if considering multifamily in the Inland Empire or outer LA County, industrial job clusters in San Gabriel Valley warrant attention as anchors for renter demand in nearby residential submarkets.

stories.title: Happier Grocery to Open Second NYC Location on the Upper East Side
stories.excerpt: A healthy grocery retailer is opening its second New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Happier Grocery has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at CSC Real Estate’s 210 East 86th Street, where it plans to open a health food store like its original one on Canal Street in the second half of 2027, according to landlord broker Avison Young. Avison Young did not immediately disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent along the nearby retail corridor of Third Avenue from East 60th to East 72nd streets was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “This lease transforms a long-vacant former movie theater space into a vibrant, wellness-focused destination that will add new energy to one of the Upper East Side’s most active retail corridors,” Avison Young’s Christian Stanton said in a statement. “Happier Grocery brings a fresh concept to the neighborhood, combining a curated, high-end grocery experience with a social atmosphere that complements the area’s strong residential base and established food retailers.” Stanton negotiated the deal on behalf of the landlord alongside Libby Hodes of Avison Young, as well as Max Swerdloff from Brand Urban. Newmark’s Brian Segall and Michael Cohen represented Happier Grocery in the deal. Happier Grocery opened its flagship location at 365 Canal Street in 2023, and has made a name for itself as a convenient stop for organic goodies. It also has a deli for hot food and a coffee bar at its Canal Street location. The grocer’s lease is the first deal to be signed at 210 East 86th Street after CSC Real Estate acquired it along with 206 East 86th Street and 205 East 85th Street for a total of $70 million in June, as Commercial Observer first reported. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Happier Grocery signs 20.5K SF lease, 210 East 86th St., Manhattan Upper East Side.
Health-focused grocer opening second NYC location; planned opening H2 2027.
Third Ave. retail corridor asking rents ~$252/SF (Q2 2026); formerly vacant theater space.
stories.summary: Happier Grocery has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at 210 East 86th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side for its second New York City location, converting a long-vacant former movie theater into a health-focused grocery and social space. The property is expected to open in the second half of 2027. The nearby Third Avenue retail corridor commanded average asking rents of $252 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, high-quality retail activation (replacing vacancy) in a prime Manhattan corridor enhances neighborhood walkability and amenity appeal, which can support multifamily rents and absorption in the Upper East Side. For TCR: continued retail densification in Manhattan's established neighborhoods validates mixed-use density and supports pre-leasing for residential components in similar corridors.

stories.title: Richard Born Part of Investor Group in BlackRock’s $245M Sale of 600 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Hotel investor Richard Born is the unnamed investor in 600 Third Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. Born joined L&L Infinite, a joint venture formed by former Silverstein Properties CEO Marty Burger and L&L Holding CEO David Levinson, as an investor in the $245 million purchase of the 42-story Midtown East office building from BlackRock, sources familiar with the deal told CO. Born now owns around 25 percent of the property, with each investor owning a roughly equal portion, a source said. Affiliates of Richard Mack’s Mack Real Estate Group, BLDG and BD Blakely were also part of the purchase. BD Blakely is an affiliate of BD Hotels, which was founded in 1986 by Born and Ira Drukier. Bloomberg first reported the sale, but did not mention Born’s involvement, reporting only that an institutional investor had teamed with L&L Infinite. The deal marks a big transformation for the office building, which BlackRock previously had a 99.5 percent stake in for roughly the past 20 years, with L&L Holding owning just 0.5 percent. Blackrock exited the deal to recycle capital, one source said. L&L Infinite and Born secured a $185 million acquisition loan from Bain Capital at closing to purchase the 1970-built property between East 39th and East 40th streets that was renovated in 2015. Newmark‘s Jordan Roeschlaub arranged the loan alongside Bain. Newmark also arranged the sale transaction with a team consisting of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger, Josh King, Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Doug Harmon. The property was 93 percent leased at the time of the deal, according to sources. Its anchor tenants include L-3 Communications, which occupies close to 59,000 square feet, along with law firms Polsinelli PC and Aaronson Rappaport Feinstein & Deutsch. Aaronson Rappaport renewed a 42,764-square-foot lease for its headquarters on the entire fifth and sixth floors in February 2025, CO first reported at the time. bullets: Richard Born, L&L Infinite, Mack Real Estate Group acquired 600 Third Ave., Manhattan for $245M.
42-story Midtown East office building; Born owns ~25% stake via L&L Infinite JV.

stories.summary: A consortium led by L&L Infinite (a joint venture of former Silverstein Properties CEO Marty Burger and L&L Holding CEO David Levinson) purchased the 42-story office building at 600 Third Avenue in Midtown East from BlackRock for $245 million. Hotel investor Richard Born joined as an investor with approximately 25% ownership, alongside Mack Real Estate Group and affiliates BLDG and BD Blakely. stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, continued acquisition of Manhattan office towers by experienced mixed-use and hospitality investors (Born, Burger, Levinson, Mack) suggests potential conversion-to-residential strategies that could unlock supply in tight NYC submarkets. For TCR: monitor institutional office repositioning in Midtown East and other secondary office nodes; conversion to residential may present future asset acquisition or JV opportunities, but regulatory, financing, and construction economics remain challenging.

stories.title: JP Morgan Chase Sells South Florida Rental for $106M
stories.excerpt: J.P. Morgan Chase sold a garden-style multifamily property in Wellington, Fla., for $105.5 million after owning it for nearly a quarter century, according to property records. TA Realty purchased the 366-unit Polo Lakes community at 1950 Polo Lake Boulevard, just north of the Mall at Wellington Green, adjacent to Route 441, in the town best known as a leading equestrian hub. Built in 2000, the 19-acre property features 27 three-story buildings, as well as a basketball court and a pool. The sale equates to about $288,000 per apartment. J.P. Morgan Chase had purchased the 530,918-square-foot property for $47.4 million in 2002. TA Realty, which specializes in multifamily and industrial assets, has been making inroads in South Florida. Last year, the Boston-based firm paid $118 million for a 300-unit property in Pembroke Pines and $193 million for a 476-unit asset in Palm Beach Gardens. On the industrial front this year, TA Realty bought an industrial park near Miami International Airport for $48 million. A spokesperson for J.P. Morgan Chase’s asset management division declined to comment, while a representative for TA Realty did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: J.P. Morgan Chase sold Polo Lakes, Wellington, FL, 366-unit garden-style property for $105.5M.
Sale price ~$288K/unit; TA Realty buyer; property built 2000, held 24 years.
Wellington location near Route 441, equestrian hub; TA Realty made $311M South FL acquisitions last year.
stories.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase sold Polo Lakes, a 366-unit garden-style multifamily community in Wellington, Florida, to Boston-based TA Realty for $105.5 million ($288,000 per unit) after holding the asset for nearly 25 years since its 2000 construction. The 19-acre property features 27 three-story buildings and sits north of the Mall at Wellington Green adjacent to Route 441. TA Realty has been actively acquiring South Florida multifamily, with $311 million in recent purchases in the region.
stories.impact: Strong South Florida multifamily signal. At $288K/unit for a stabilized, fully built-out garden-style asset in Wellington (a secondary suburban market north of West Palm Beach), pricing reflects compressed cap rates and sustained institutional appetite for South Florida multifamily. For TCR: South Florida multifamily fundamentals remain solid (population in-migration, limited supply, rent growth), but valuations are tightening and competition is intense. Prioritize land and development in emerging secondary submarkets (Broward County west, St. Lucie, Palm Beach County inland) to achieve development returns before cost inflation and scarcity value offset project economics.
